headline: Startup Modeled End to End, Cold Plasma to the Frozen Point
summary: Kronos has run its breeder's full startup sequence in the digital twin and confirmed the modeled path reaches the frozen design point without breaking the machine's structural margin.

headline: Shutdown and Ramp-Down Modeled Without a Forced Disruption
summary: Kronos checked the reverse of the startup path, bringing plasma current and centrepost field back down cleanly, rather than assuming a machine that starts well also stops well.

headline: Gate Closed: MetroVolt's Data-Center Configuration Fits Its Shared Burner Core
summary: One low-neutron D-³He core, two housings — Kronos has confirmed MetroVolt's data-center configuration fits its output characteristics independently of Aegis.

headline: Gate closed: direct-DC power reaches the campus boundary clean
summary: Kronos has closed the de-risking gate confirming MetroVolt can deliver its direct energy-conversion output as clean direct current at the campus interface, without an unnecessary AC conversion stage.

headline: Kronos Maps the Steady-State Operating Window Around Its Frozen Design Point
summary: The frozen breeder point sits inside its own mapped operating window with margin on the structural side, but the map does not paper over the one MHD figure that remains unresolved.

headline: Radial-Build Analysis Finds Recoverable Margin in the Breeder's Center-Stack
summary: A layer-by-layer review of the center-stack finds roughly 2 centimeters of radial space that current minimums do not actually require.

headline: Neutron-activation profile computed for the breeder's first wall
summary: Kronos has traced where radiation damage accumulates fastest across the breeder's neutron-facing structure, ahead of publishing its waste-classification estimate.

headline: Kronos Closes De-Risking Gate on Its Staged Fuel-Cycle Plan
summary: Rather than assuming fleet-scale tritium supply appears instantly, Kronos has staged how tritium bred by a first machine funds startup inventory for the next one.

headline: Gate Closed: Isotope Yield Checks Out Against the Neutron Budget
summary: Kronos has confirmed its breeder's neutron economy can support isotope-services output on top of self-sufficient tritium breeding, without eroding the breeding margin.

headline: Waste Classification Estimated From the Activation Profile
summary: Kronos ran an early waste-classification estimate from its computed activation profile, and found the low-neutron burner and the full-spectrum breeder tell two different stories, reported separately rather than blended.

headline: Modeled Thermal Path Closes Across a Thousand-Kelvin-Plus Gradient
summary: From a 20-kelvin magnet network to plasma-facing surfaces exposed to 85 megawatts of fusion power, Hyperion's end-to-end thermal balance checks out without forcing a redesign.

headline: Gate closed: the low-neutron safety case stands
summary: Kronos has closed the de-risking gate on its burner's safety case, grounded in an aneutronic-dominant reaction that holds the neutron fraction to 5.44% and simplifies shielding as a direct consequence.

headline: Kronos Closes Manufacturability Gate on a Key Centrepost Component
summary: Kronos says a design that can't be built isn't a design, and it has now confirmed a key component in the breeder's centrepost can be fabricated to the tolerances its structural and shielding gates assume.

headline: Gate Closed: Breeder's Assembly Sequence Clears Digital-Twin Check
summary: A digital-twin walkthrough confirms the machine's components fit and clear each other in the order the build plan calls for.

headline: Fuel-cycle inventory balanced against losses and decay
summary: Kronos checked its breeder's tritium production against operating losses, radioactive decay, and next-machine startup needs over a modeled campaign, and the margin holds.

headline: Kronos Bounds Tritium Retention in the Breeder's First Wall
summary: Not all bred tritium reaches the fuel-cycle loop; Kronos checked how much stays trapped in first-wall material and found the breeding margin still holds.

headline: Blanket Breeding Uniformity Checked Across Near-4π Coverage
summary: Kronos checked whether a local cold spot in blanket coverage could hide behind an otherwise-healthy average breeding ratio, and found the modeled rate holds even across the blanket.

headline: Plasma-Facing Material Checked Against Combined Design Loads
summary: Kronos tested a candidate first-wall material against neutron fluence and thermal load together, not separately, because that combined case is the one that actually happens in operation.

headline: One Gate Left Open on the Record: Helium-3 Doesn't Close Indigenously
summary: Kronos names a gap in its own de-risking Register rather than closing it early: helium-3 co-production carries strategic value but is not yet a standalone product.

headline: MHD Operating Limit Located — With the β_N Caveat Named
summary: Kronos has located the modeled MHD stability boundary for the breeder's frozen design point, and is naming an unresolved normalized-beta comparison plainly rather than rounding it into a clean pass.

headline: Kronos Bounds Disruption Loads Within the Centrepost's Existing Structural Margin
summary: A fast plasma-current dump has to survive on the structure even when the plasma itself doesn't; Kronos says its modeled worst case fits inside the margin already validated for normal operation.

headline: Breeder Control Policy Validated in the Twin Before Hardware
summary: Startup, steady-state, and disruption-adjacent scenarios all held within the modeled operating window built around the frozen design point.

headline: Digital twin reproduces the frozen design point against independent codes
summary: Kronos benchmarked its digital twin against the CGYRO turbulence dataset and its own frozen design-point anchors, and found the twin holds rather than drifts.

headline: Independent Environment Confirms Kronos's Published Reproduction
summary: A third, independent run of the AI + Quantum method deposit reached the same published figure, outside the environments used at deposit time.

headline: Sensitivity Analysis Narrows What Actually Moves the Design Point
summary: Kronos ranked the inputs behind its frozen breeder design point and found a small set of parameters accounts for most of the sensitivity.

headline: A Prior Assumption Revised on New Modeling Evidence
summary: Kronos revised one input assumption behind its canonical anchors this cycle, and is saying so in public rather than updating the number without comment.

headline: Kronos Names an Open Gap Before It Bites: Helium-3 Isn't a Standalone Product Yet
summary: The company draws a clear line between tritium, its base product, and helium-3, a strategically valuable byproduct that does not yet close its own supply chain.

headline: A Result That Didn't Clear, Reported Honestly
summary: A normalized-beta comparison against the design's reference stability limit did not resolve in Kronos's favor this cycle — and the company is publishing that outcome rather than rounding it into a pass.

headline: Kronos Cross-Checks Breeder and Burner Assumptions, Finds Them Consistent
summary: Hyperion and the Aegis/MetroVolt burner are different machines, but they share a conductor, cryogenic, and structural basis, and Kronos says neither program has drifted from the other's version of it.

headline: Kronos Publishes Full Design Paper on the Tritium Breeding Blanket
summary: The paper behind Hyperion's fuel-factory shell lays out the geometry, neutron multiplication, and coverage that turn a fusion neutron into bred tritium.

headline: Net self-sufficiency case published as a standalone paper
summary: Kronos has given its breeder's net tritium-breeding result its own citable paper and DOI, the claim that turns Hyperion from a fusion device into a fuel factory that feeds itself.

headline: Kronos Names a Neutron-Tolerance Gap in Its NV-Diamond Sensing Package
key_anchor: NV 0.189 pT/√Hz @125 kHz (gated) ; NV neutron tol ~39× short (open)
summary: The same magnetometer package that holds strong field sensitivity falls roughly 39 times short of the neutron-tolerance target it needs for in-vessel deployment.

headline: Net Tritium Breeding Margin Confirmed by Divertor Configuration: 1.12 SN / 1.07 DN
summary: Kronos states its tritium-breeding margin separately for each divertor geometry rather than averaging them, because a plant committing to one geometry commits to a different fuel-cycle margin.

headline: Transport: Modeling the Edge and Scrape-Off Layer
summary: A second, independent code takes over where the core turbulence model leaves off, checking whether Hyperion's negative-triangularity edge behaves as steadily as designed at the boundary itself.

headline: Negative-Triangularity Shaping Paper Published for Hyperion's Outward-Pointing D-Shape
summary: The physics case for pointing the plasma boundary the 'wrong' way, and why it steadies both the edge and the divertor, is now in a completed paper.

headline: Center-Stack Shielding and Engineering Paper Published
summary: Kronos has published the shielding and engineering paper for the center stack, the column that carries the toroidal field coil through the plasma core and has to survive years of 14.1 MeV neutron bombardment while doing it.

headline: Kronos Reports Fused Quench Detector Reaching AUC 0.992 in Simulation
summary: Combining digital-twin state estimates with simulated magnet sensor telemetry lets a classifier flag a pre-quench state earlier than either data source could alone, at least on the modeled test set.

headline: Kronos Cross-Checks Turbulence Results With a Second Gyrokinetic Code
summary: Every major confinement claim rests on one code, CGYRO, so Kronos is running a second, independently built solver against it.

headline: Design locked: the control-sensor network
summary: Kronos has fixed the sensor architecture feeding its plasma-control system, built on published results in quench detection, magnetometry, and safety clamping, with one gap still open.

headline: Kronos Publishes Paper on Five-Channel Direct Energy Conversion
summary: The burner converts charged exhaust straight into current across five stacked conversion channels, reaching an efficiency of 0.49 with no steam cycle.

headline: NV-Diamond Magnetometry Reaches 0.189 pT/√Hz at 125 kHz
summary: Kronos's NV-diamond sensor package hits a sensitivity figure strong enough to feed its quench-detection work, while its radiation tolerance for in-vessel use still falls short of qualification.

headline: Control-Barrier-Function Clamp Cuts Safety Violations to 0/100
summary: Adding a mathematical safety clamp to Hyperion's control policy took its violation rate across 100 modeled scenarios from roughly half down to zero.

headline: Analysis Traces the Burner's Energy Path From Plasma Exhaust to Delivered Power
summary: A five-channel direct-conversion stack turns charged particles into electricity without a steam cycle — Kronos has now accounted for every stage between plasma and the outlet.

headline: Thermal: the cold-side energy books
summary: A cryogenic heat-balance analysis sizes the closed-cycle cooling system for the breeder's magnet set, accounting for every heat load into a system held near 20 K.

headline: Kronos Publishes Cryogenic Architecture Paper Covering Both Field Targets
summary: The closed-cycle cryoplant that keeps both Kronos machines' REBCO coils superconducting near 20 K now has its full architecture paper public, covering both field targets under one shared engineering basis.

headline: Kronos Publishes Vacuum-Vessel Structural and Thermal Paper
summary: A 1-D thermal model paired with stress evaluation under normal and off-normal loading finds the breeder's outer shell holds within its design envelope.

headline: Divertor and exhaust-handling paper published
summary: Kronos has published how the breeder channels its highest heat-flux surface, with negative triangularity aimed at steadier, not just lower-peak, loading over a pulse.

headline: Kronos Publishes Component-by-Component Lifetime Analysis
summary: Rather than one blanket figure for the whole machine, Kronos assigns each major component an expected service life against the specific mechanism that will wear it out.

headline: Reliability: How Often the Machine Needs Service
summary: Kronos has built its maintenance-interval planning directly from component-lifetime analysis, sequenced to minimize downtime across a future fleet of serial units.

headline: First-Wall Materials Under 14 MeV Neutrons — Paper Published
summary: Kronos has published its neutron-survivability paper for the single most demanding surface in the machine: the first wall facing the D-T plasma directly.

headline: Tandem-Mirror End-Plug Physics Paper Published for the Burner Line
summary: Instead of a closed torus, Kronos's D-³He burner confines plasma with electrostatic potential at each end — a completed paper documents the physics behind its 26.49-tesla plug field.

headline: Plug-Density Operating Point Stated in the Open — Paper Published
summary: Kronos has published a dedicated paper on central-cell plug density, the tandem mirror's hardest operating requirement, rather than folding it into a broader design document.

headline: Kronos Publishes Sensitivity Analysis on How Robust Its Frozen Design Point Really Is
summary: A frozen design point is a single set of numbers; Kronos's new analysis asks how far each input can move before Q and the breeding margin drift outside acceptable bounds.

headline: Kronos Publishes Analysis of Control-System Disturbance Rejection
summary: Holding a target state against sensor noise and unmodeled dynamics is a distinct question from whether a safety clamp holds hard limits, and Kronos is answering both separately.

headline: Low-neutron D-3He reaction economy paper published
summary: Kronos has published why the burner's near-aneutronic fuel cycle reshapes shielding, activation, and structural fluence across the machine's life.

headline: Kronos Publishes Helium-3 Co-Production Pathway Paper
summary: The breeder's highest-value by-product gets its own pathway paper, framed against tritium as the platform's actual bankable product.

headline: Neutron-Economy Materials Platform Paper Published
summary: Kronos has published the public case for Hyperion as a materials platform, arguing its resource stream of tritium, helium-3, and high-flux neutrons stands on its own, independent of any electricity export.

headline: AI/ML Plasma Control Paper (KRONOS-CTRL) Published
summary: Kronos has published the paper positioning its control system as a first-class subsystem across both breeder and burner, not an add-on layered over the plasma physics.

headline: Paper Published on Catching Vertical-Displacement Events in Microseconds, Not Seconds
summary: A vertical displacement event can outrun a human operator; Kronos has published a control approach designed to catch it on the plasma's own timescale.

headline: Load-Following and Grid Integration Paper Published
summary: A new paper models how the burner line's direct-DC output tracks a real, variable grid demand profile — a case MetroVolt's data-center application depends on directly.

headline: Kronos Publishes Digital-Twin Architecture and Validation Paper
summary: The component-by-component model Kronos uses to validate designs and train control policy before any hardware exists now has its full architecture and validation methodology on the record.

headline: Kronos Publishes Gyrokinetic Turbulence Paper Behind Its CGYRO Results
summary: The full methodology behind the negative-triangularity confinement claim is now public, not just the headline number.

headline: Edge and scrape-off-layer transport paper published
summary: Kronos has published the physics governing the plasma boundary between the breeder's confined core and its divertor, connecting directly to its negative-triangularity and divertor design results.

headline: Kronos Publishes MHD Stability and Operating-Limits Paper
summary: The paper defining where the breeder's operating window ends also names an unresolved gap in normalized beta rather than picking the more favorable figure.

headline: Magnet Quench and Protection Paper Published
summary: Kronos has published the protection architecture that detects a superconducting magnet quench early and routes stored energy out safely before it can damage the coil.

headline: Fuel-Cycle Staging Strategy Paper Published
summary: Tritium's own 12.3-year half-life is why Kronos stages its fuel cycle rather than building a single inventory all at once; the strategy paper explaining why is now published.

headline: Isotope Production and Neutron-Services Paper Published for the Breeder Platform
summary: A high-flux 14.1 MeV neutron source generates more than tritium — Kronos has published the case for using neutron irradiation services as an addition to, not a substitute for, its core breeding mission.

headline: Medical-Isotope Pathway Paper Published
summary: Kronos has published a paper on a pathway toward medical isotope production, a co-located application of the same high-flux neutron source the breeder uses to breed its primary fuel.

headline: Kronos Publishes Reproducibility and Open-Evaluator Methods Paper
summary: Kronos has published the methods paper meant to make every result in its series executable, not just citable: a design point isn't just stated as a number, it's re-derivable.

headline: Kronos Publishes Methodology Paper Behind Its De-Risking Register
summary: The paper explains how a fusion program turns into a set of individually checkable claims, and how an open gate gets named rather than hidden.

headline: Aegis defense-burner configuration paper published
summary: Kronos has published how its shared burner core and five-channel direct-energy-conversion stack are packaged into Aegis, a fixed forward-base generator, not a naval or mobile platform.

headline: Kronos Publishes MetroVolt Data-Center Burner Configuration Paper
summary: The configuration paper for the data-center housing built on the shared burner core describes direct-DC output built to match how modern data centers already run power internally.

headline: Thermal Management Across the Cryo–Plasma Gradient: Paper Published
summary: Kronos has published the end-to-end thermal path connecting a 20 K magnet coil to a fusion-temperature plasma core across centimeters of shielding.

headline: Neutron Fluence and Shielding Budget for the Breeder Core — Paper Published
summary: Kronos has published the fluence-budgeting paper that sizes every shielding layer between the plasma and the outside world, working outward from the first wall the centrepost already shares a load case with.

headline: One Paper Compares Radiation Activation Across Both the Breeder and the Burner
summary: The breeder runs full D-T fusion; the burner holds its neutron fraction to 5.44%. A new paper works the activation and materials-lifetime question for both machines side by side.

headline: First-Wall and Divertor Survivability Under Steady-State Load — Paper Published
summary: A new paper shows how the breeder's negative-triangularity shaping keeps first-wall and divertor loading steady rather than pulsed, the difference between components rated for years and components rated for one transient.

headline: Kronos Publishes Pressure-Performance and Beta-Limit Paper, Names One Open Item
summary: How hard the breeder's plasma can be pressurized before instabilities set the limit is now a published paper, and it does not hide the one beta figure Kronos hasn't yet resolved.

headline: Kronos Publishes Paper on Sustaining the Breeder's Plasma Current
summary: Holding 9.66 megamperes through a pulse takes more than reaching it once, and the current-drive paper documents how Hyperion does it.

headline: Feeding the burn: pellet-fueling paper published for Hyperion
summary: Kronos has published how it plans to keep the breeder's plasma density in range over a pulse, replacing fuel at the rate the core actually consumes it.

headline: Kronos Publishes Diagnostics Suite Paper, Turning Plasma Into Data
summary: The sensing layer that control and every other subsystem depends on is documented in full, with NV-diamond magnetometry confirmed to a specific sensitivity figure.

headline: Proof Before the AI Touches Plasma: Control-Validation Methodology
summary: Kronos requires any learned control policy to clear a hard safety clamp before it can act near a live plasma, and the clamp held violations to zero in testing.

headline: The Modeling Stack Behind Every Design Claim — Architecture Paper
summary: Kronos has documented, end to end, which code does which job and how results move between stages, the architecture underneath every number the company has frozen so far.

headline: Verification Paper Checks Kronos's Own Codes Against the Field's Established Tools
summary: The negative-triangularity confinement claim was already benchmarked against nonlinear CGYRO — a new paper extends that same external cross-checking across the rest of the modeling stack.

headline: The Safety Case for a Low-Neutron Burner — Paper Published
summary: Kronos has published the formal safety case for its D-³He burner, grounded in fusion's inherent shutdown property and an aneutronic-dominant reaction that keeps the neutron fraction to 5.44%.

headline: Kronos Publishes Waste and Activation Profile Across Its Fleet
summary: Kronos has published a full accounting of what its machines leave behind, not just what they produce while running, comparing the breeder's full neutron output against the burner's low-neutron design.

headline: Kronos Publishes Site-Level Environmental Characterization Paper
summary: A public-safe look at footprint and land use for a breeder or burner installation stays scoped to characterization, not an impact assessment.

headline: A short companion note ties confinement to heating at the frozen design point
summary: Not every Kronos result needs a full paper. This addendum links the confinement-scaling and current-drive work already published, at the breeder's Q = 3.076 operating point.

headline: Kronos Publishes Standalone Data Descriptor for Blanket Neutronics
summary: Geometry, source terms, and multiplication assumptions behind the breeding blanket are now documented well enough for the underlying neutron-transport runs to be re-derived.

headline: Turbulent-Transport Run Data Documented as a Standalone Descriptor
summary: Kronos has released the run-level detail behind its negative-triangularity confinement claim, covering the specific gyrokinetic simulations rather than just their conclusions.

headline: Digital-Twin Validation Data Documented as a Standalone Descriptor
summary: The dataset Kronos uses to check its digital twin against physics codes and benchmarks now has its own published descriptor, so the check itself is on the record, not just the claim that it happened.

headline: New Note Shows the Assumptions Behind Kronos's Frozen Design Numbers, Not Just the Numbers
summary: A companion document lays out how key inputs were chosen and how sensitive the program's headline figures are to reasonable variation in them.

headline: The Work We Haven't Closed, Named: An Open-Gates Companion Note
summary: Alongside its closed gates, Kronos publishes a companion note naming what hasn't resolved yet — a sensor-tolerance gap, a structural margin still to recover, and an unresolved stability comparison — plainly and without rounding them away.

headline: Kronos Publishes Power-Quality Paper for the Burner's Direct-DC Interface
summary: Skipping a thermal cycle changes what shows up at the boundary between the burner and whatever it powers; Kronos has now published how that direct-DC interface is conditioned for a data-center or forward-base load.
